Akagisan|ja|富士見町赤城山|qid=Q22125907}} area. It is considered a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}}) and a disputed {{ill|Second Shrine of Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国二宮}}. Its former Rank under the modern shrine Ranking system was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|勢多郡誌編纂委員会|1958|p=1230}}<ref>Gunma Prefecture, "Jōmō Taikan," Kankodō, 1934, [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1224435/1/195 p.278]</ref>.
This shrine is a center of Mount Akagi worship, enshrining Akagi Daimyōjin, {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375}}, and several other deities. The sacred bodies are Mount Akagi and the lakes Ōnuma and Konuma at its summit.<ref name="rekimachi" />
While the official name is '''Akagi Shrine''', it is also called '''Daidō Akagi Shrine''' (大洞赤城神社) to distinguish it from other shrines of the same name. It is considered one of the main shrines among the approximately 300 Akagi Shrines found throughout Japan, especially concentrated in the {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kantō region}}.

Its former shrine Ranking under the Modern Shrine Ranking System was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Murasha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}{{Sfn|勢多郡誌編纂委員会|1958|p=1230}}<ref>Gunma Prefecture, “Jōmō Daikan”, Kankodo, 1934, [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1224435/1/195 p.278]</ref>.
It is a shrine of Mount Akagi faith, enshrining {{ill|Akagi Shrines|ja|赤城大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 赤城神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11635468}}, {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375}}, among several other deities, and it considers Mount Akagi and the lakes on its summit—the large lake (Ōno) and the small lake (Kono)—as its sacred object.<ref name="rekimachi" />
Although its official name is '''Akagi Shrine''', to distinguish it from other {{ill|Akagi Shrines|ja|赤城神社}}, it is also called '''Daidō Akagi Shrine''' (Daidō–). It is one of what is presumed to be the main shrines among the approximately 300 Akagi Shrines nationwide, especially in the {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kanto Region}}.

== History ==
[[File:MountAkagi.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{ill|Mount Akagi|arz|جبل مونت اكاجى|ca|Mont Akagi|ceb|Akagi San|cs|Akagi (sopka)|de|Akagi (Vulkan)|es|Monte Akagi|eu|Akagi mendia|fr|Mont Akagi|id|Gunung Akagi|ja|赤城山|ko|아카기산|my|အခဂိတောင်|pl|Akagi (szczyt)|pnb|ٹلہ اکاگی|pt|Monte Akagi|ru|Акаги (вулкан)|sk|Akagi (sopka)|tr|Akagi Dağı|uz|Akagi togʻi|vi|Núi Akagi|zh|赤城山 (日本)|qid=Q415251|lt=Mount Akagi}} (object of worship)]]
[[File:akagiyama_ono.jpg|thumb|right|Mount Akagi Summit<br/>Our shrine is located on the central peninsula ({{ill|Kotori-ga-shima|ja|小鳥ヶ島}}). The area with the building at the far left of the lake is Daidō, and the mountain at the far right is {{ill|Jizōdake|ja|神庫山}} (Jizōdake).]]
== Founding ==
The founding is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375}} enshrined the spirits of the mountain and marsh when he came to rule over {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|qid=Q1054838|lt=Kamino}}, and later, during the reigns of {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|en|Emperor Ingyō|qid=Q349258|lt=Emperor Ingyō}} and {{ill|Emperor Yōmei|en|Emperor Yōmei|qid=Q349281|lt=Emperor Yōmei}}, the shrine buildings were established.{{Sfn|富士見村誌編纂委員会|1979|pp=631-632}}
It is said that at the time of the initial enshrinement the deity was venerated on the mid-slope of {{ill|Hokurayama|ja|神庫山}} (later known as Jizōdake), but in {{ill|806|en|806|qid=Q30021|lt=806}} (the first year of {{ill|Daidō|en|Daidō|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}}), it was relocated to the southern bank of {{ill|Ono|ja|大沼 (赤城山)|lt=Ōnuma|lt_ja=大沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnuma (Mount Akagi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11437111}} (Ono) at the current old Daidō shrine grounds, and on the bank of the small marsh, the {{ill|Kono Shrine|ja|小沼宮|lt=Konogū}} (later known as {{ill|Toyouke Shrine|ja|豊受神社}}) was built.<ref name="由緒書">Shrine tradition record.</ref> It is said that, because of the era name, the area around the shrine came to be known as “Daidō”, and hence it is also called “Daidō Akagi Shrine”.<ref name="由緒書"/> However, it is also said that “Daidō” was written as “Daidō” (大堂), and that a hall once stood on the summit.<ref>“Akagi Shrine”.</ref>
It is said that since ancient times the mountain’s {{ill|Akagi Shrines|ja|赤城大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 赤城神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11635468}} and the marsh deity {{ill|Akanauma Ōkami|ja|赤沼大神}} were enshrined, and that mirrors once used for worship were discovered in the lake.
== Heian to Sengoku Period ==
In {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|qid=Q1151168|lt=Rokukokushi}}, there are several records of bestowing shrine Ranks upon “Akagi Shrine”, and in the mid-{{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian Period}} text {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} an entry appears for the “Akagi Shrine of {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|qid=Q1054838|lt=Ueno Province}} {{ill|Seta District, Gunma|en|Seta District, Gunma|qid=Q2324302|lt=Setagun}}” as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meishin Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9610964}}, recognized as a {{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社|lt=Ronsha}}}}. Among the Ronsha, besides our shrine at the summit of Mount Akagi, there are also the mountainside shrine {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社 (前橋市三夜沢町)|lt=Sanyazawa Akagi Shrine|lt_ja=三夜沢赤城神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanyazawa Akagi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11635467}} and the foothill shrine {{ill|Ninomiya Akagi Shrine|ja|二宮赤城神社}}; however, this remains uncertain.
Our shrine is presumed to be the mountain shrine (Yamamiya) of Akagi Shrine. The mountain shrine developed during the {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}} period when {{ill|Yamabushi|ja|修験者|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shugensha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山伏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2309838}} ascended various sacred mountains for training, making these peaks centers of their faith. Moreover, the rise of the samurai government led to a decline in the power of the imperial court and provincial governors, which in turn reduced the economic strength of the village shrine (Satemiya). As a result, while the shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} (the inner shrine) declined, the influence of the mountain shrine and the central shrine (Chūsha) along the pilgrimage routes grew.
In the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō Period}}, the work {{ill|Shintōshū|en|Shintōshū|qid=Q2616931|lt=Shintōshū}} contains three legends concerning {{ill|Akagi Shrines|ja|赤城大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 赤城神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11635468}}, with accounts of enshrinements at both Ōnuma and Konoma (see {{ill|Akagi Shrines|ja|赤城神社#神道集|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine#Shintōshū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11635468}}). This is the oldest historical source pinpointing the location of Akagi Shrine.<ref name="由緒書"/> From this description, it is interpreted that at the time the text was composed the marsh was the center of worship.<ref>“Sekai Daihyakka Jiten” ({{ill|Heibonsha|en|Heibonsha|qid=Q11482108|lt=Heibonsha}}), entry on Mount Akagi.</ref>
== Edo Period ==
Daidō Akagi Shrine first appears in historical records during the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo Period}}. In {{ill|1601|en|1601|qid=Q6725|lt=1601}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}}), {{ill|Sakai Shigetada|ja|酒井重忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakai Shigetada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5369481}}—lord of {{ill|Maebashi Castle|en|Maebashi Castle|qid=Q10898917|lt=Umabashi (Maebashi) Castle}}—entered service and fervently worshipped the Daidō Akagi Shrine facing the {{ill|Kimon|ja|鬼門}}, a practice followed by successive feudal lords. Shigetada petitioned the shogunate for a reconstruction of the “Shōichii Akagi Daimyōjin / Akagi Shrine”, and the work was completed. The next lord, {{ill|Sakai Tadayo|en|Sakai Tadayo|qid=Q1065113|lt=Sakai Tadayoshi}}, enshrined {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu-kō}} in the side hall, and the Sakai family designated the abbot of Juunen-ji in Maebashi.
In {{ill|1641|en|1641|qid=Q6907|lt=1641}} (the 18th year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei}}), the shrine buildings were entirely destroyed by lightning and rebuilt by {{ill|Sakai Tadakiyo|en|Sakai Tadakiyo|qid=Q7402769|lt=Sakai Tadayoshi}}.{{Sfn|富士見村誌編纂委員会|1979|pp=631-632}} Originally, the combined worship of the mountain deity and {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|ja|東照大権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōshō Daigongen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳川家康|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q171977}} ({{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}) attracted devotion not only from the shogunate but also from many feudal lords nationwide. The “Yamakirihiki Festival” on the eighth day of Uzuki, celebrated as the “Akagi Pilgrimage”, reportedly drew a vast number of worshipers from across the {{ill|Kantō|ja|関東|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11655841}} region. During this period, branch shrines were established throughout the area under shogunal protection.
During the {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei Period}}, a dispute arose between Sanyazawa Akagi Shrine and Daidō Akagi Shrine over the usage of the terms “Honsha” and “Honkū”. In {{ill|1798|en|1798|qid=Q7823|lt=1798}} (the 10th year of Kansei), the {{ill|Yoshida Family|ja|吉田家|lt=Yoshida family}}—which had been granted the Rank of Shōichii at Sanyazawa Akagi Shrine—was asked by Daidō Akagi Shrine for a donation recorded as “Shōichii”. The Yoshida family consulted with the Sanyazawa side, who rejected the request. However, the following year, the {{ill|Minister of Divinities|ja|神祇伯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minister of Divinities|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17210025}} and {{ill|Shirakawa family|ja|白川家|lt=Shirakawa Hakuō Family|lt_ja=白川伯王家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 白川伯王家|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11579697}}, who were at odds with the Yoshida family, offered a document bearing the inscription “Honsha”/“Honkū” for “Ueno Province Sōsha Daidō Akagi Shrine”. This document was to be unveiled during the annual Senju Kannon exhibition held in Maebashi. The Sanyazawa side strongly protested, and in {{ill|1800|en|1800|qid=Q6875|lt=1800}} (the 12th year of Kansei) the abbot of Daidō Akagi Shrine at Juunen-ji together with the Shirakawa Hakuō family initiated litigation—including a request to halt the unveiling. The lord of the {{ill|Kawagoe Domain|en|Kawagoe Domain|qid=Q3034465|lt=Kawagoe Domain}}, Matsudaira, intervened as mediator; the disputed document was sealed while the scheduled unveiling at Daidō proceeded as planned. Nevertheless, the controversy continued, and in {{ill|1802|en|1802|qid=Q6883|lt=1802}} (the 2nd year of {{ill|Kyōwa|en|Kyōwa|qid=Q960763|lt=Kyōwa}}) the Sanyazawa side appealed to the {{ill|Jisha-bugyō|en|Jisha-bugyō|qid=Q1036279|lt=Temple and Shrine Magistrate}} of the shogunate, and a national resolution was mandated. Ultimately, an accord was reached in {{ill|1816|en|1816|qid=Q6953|lt=1816}} (the 13th year of {{ill|Bunka|en|Bunka|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}}) whereby the document was deposited in the inner shrine and the usage of the inscription was determined by mutual agreement (as recorded in “Miyagi Mura-shi”).
== From the Meiji Period Onwards ==
Due to the {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|qid=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu Kishaku}} of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the shrine was separated from Juunen-ji and a new priest was appointed from among locals promoting anti-Buddhist reforms. Furthermore, plans were proposed to rebuild the shrine buildings—which had deteriorated over more than three centuries under Mount Akagi’s harsh climate—but these were never realized. Between the 20th and 43rd years of the Meiji era, several shrines within Mount Akagi, including the {{ill|Toyouke Shrine at Konoma|ja|小沼の豊受神社}}, the {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine on Kotori-ga-shima|ja|小鳥ヶ島の厳島神社}}, and the {{ill|Takakami Shrine on Kurohi Mountain Summit|ja|黒檜山頂の高於神社}}, were merged.<ref name="由緒書"/>{{Sfn|富士見村誌編纂委員会|1954|pp=472-474}}
Furthermore, under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Murasha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. There was even an initiative to combine the three shrines—Sanyazawa, Daidō, and Ninomiya—into a {{ill|Kokuhei Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, but this never materialized due to the end of the war.
In {{ill|1970|en|1970|qid=Q2474|lt=1970}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa}} 45), the shrine was relocated to the current site on Kotori-ga-shima (the former site of Itsukushima Shrine), and a new shrine building was constructed that still stands today. At that time, opposition movements arose, claiming that the environment of Kotori-ga-shima was being destroyed.
In {{ill|2006|en|2006|qid=Q2021|lt=2006}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18), a major restoration was undertaken on the occasion of the Daidō Shrine Relocation 1200th Anniversary Festival.
== Shrine Ranks ==
* According to the {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|qid=Q1151168|lt=Rokukokushi}}, there are records of bestowing shrine Ranks upon “Akagi Shrine” (though theories exist that differ for shrines other than this one).
** In the 6th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|en|Jōwa (Heian period)|qid=Q1075605|lt=Shōwa}} ({{ill|839|en|839|qid=Q23874|lt=839}}) in June, a lowering to Junior Fifth Rank was recorded in <nowiki>“Zoku Nihon Kōki”</nowiki> ({{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}}).
** In the 9th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|Jōgan}} ({{ill|867|en|867|qid=Q30347|lt=867}}) on June 20, a promotion from Junior Fifth Rank Upper to Senior Fifth Rank Lower was recorded in <nowiki>“Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku”</nowiki> ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}).
** In the 11th year of {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōtoku}} ({{ill|869|en|869|qid=Q23917|lt=869}}) on December 25, Senior Fifth Rank Upper was conferred (as per <nowiki>“Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku”</nowiki>).
** In the 16th year of {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōtoku}} ({{ill|874|en|874|qid=Q23843|lt=874}}) on March 14, a demotion to Junior Fourth Rank Lower was recorded ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}).
** In the 4th year of {{ill|Gangyō|en|Gangyō|qid=Q747451|lt=Genkei}} ({{ill|880|en|880|qid=Q23618|lt=880}}) on May 25, a promotion to Junior Fourth Rank Upper was recorded ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}) – the inscription is rendered as either “Akagi Ishigami” or “Akagi Numagami”.<ref>Variations in manuscripts result in either “Akagi Ishigami” or “Akagi Numagami”.</ref>
* After the {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|qid=Q1151168|lt=Rokukokushi}} period:
** Around the 3rd year of {{ill|Chōgen|en|Chōgen|qid=Q1193557|lt=Chōgen}} ({{ill|1030|en|1030|qid=Q19301|lt=1030}}), Senior First Rank was recorded in <nowiki>“Ueno-koku Kōtai Jitsuroku-chō”</nowiki>.
** Senior First Rank is also recorded in <nowiki>“Ueno-koku Shinmyōchō”</nowiki> – the inscription being “Akagi Daimyōjin”.<ref/>
== Shrine facilities ==
== Kotori-ga-shima (Current Shrine Grounds) ==
The shrine grounds were relocated from the old Daidō site in 1970, and the construction of the shrine building at that time is recorded on the “Akagi Shrine Construction Donation Commemorative Stele”.<ref name="rekimachi">{{Cite web|Language=Japanese|title=III Akagi Mountain Faith and the Historical Scenic Beauty Seen in the South Foothill Settlements|url=https://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/material/files/group/59/rekimachi_2shou_3.pdf|website=Maebashi City|accessdate=2025-02-04}}</ref>
On Kotori-ga-shima, there is an archaeological site known as the “Kotori-ga-shima Ruins” from the Nanboku-chō period. From beneath a pagoda bearing an inscription dated to the 5th year of {{ill|Ōan|en|Ōan|qid=Q1146245|lt=Ōan era}} ({{ill|1372|en|1372|qid=Q6258|lt=1372}}), which indicates the deposition of a Lotus Sutra, fragments of a copper scripture cylinder and ten mirrors were unearthed. These mirrors, along with the pagoda and the remnants of the scripture cylinder, have been designated as cultural properties by Gunma Prefecture.<ref>[http://www.manabi.pref.gunma.jp/bunkazai/g614157.htm Kotori-ga-shima Excavated Mirror] (Gunma Prefectural Lifelong Learning Center).</ref><ref>[http://www.gunmaibun.org/cgi-bin/iseki/database.cgi?cmd=dp&num=22845&dp= Kotori-ga-shima Ruins] (Gunma Prefecture Buried Cultural Properties Investigation Group).</ref>

== Others ==
* Konoma Ruins
:: An archaeological site at the bottom of the small marsh where deposited mirrors have been found, dating from the late Heian period to the Edo period.<ref>[http://www.gunmaibun.org/cgi-bin/iseki/database.cgi?cmd=dp&num=22846&dp= Konoma Ruins] (Gunma Prefecture Buried Cultural Properties Investigation Group).</ref>
* Great Torii (Maebashi, Fujimi Town, Kogure, {{ウィキ座標|36|26|44.91|N|139|05|48.69|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|位置|name=大鳥居}})
:: Located at the Kogure intersection at the foot of the mountain. Height: 21.3 m; Width: 28 m.
:: The original first torii, predating the current structure, stands at {{ill|Kogure Shrine|ja|小暮神社}} to the northeast of the intersection. This torii was installed at the mountain trail entrance in the 4th year of {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei}} ({{ill|1784|en|1784|qid=Q7752|lt=1784}}). It was later relocated to Daidō due to the construction of the Akagi toll road in the Showa era, but severe weather forced its return to Kogure.<ref>According to the explanatory stone at Kogure Shrine.</ref>

[[File:小鳥が島出土鏡.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Kotori-ga-shima Excavated Mirror}}{{small|displayed at {{ill|Gunma Prefectural Museum of History|en|Gunma Prefectural Museum of History|qid=Q20982941|lt=Gunma Prefectural Museum of History}}.}}]]
* Kotori-ga-shima Excavated Mirror (with pagoda and remnants of a scripture cylinder) (archaeological material) – Held by {{ill|Gunma Prefectural Museum of History|en|Gunma Prefectural Museum of History|qid=Q20982941|lt=Gunma Prefectural Museum of History}}. Designated on September 20, 1977 (Showa 52). The pagoda bears an inscription from the 5th year of {{ill|Ōan|en|Ōan|qid=Q1146245|lt=Ōan era}} ({{ill|1372|en|1372|qid=Q6258|lt=1372}}), and during its relocation the remnants of a scripture cylinder and ten deposited mirrors were unearthed.{{Sfn|富士見村誌編纂委員会|1979|pp=631-632}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=県指定文化財一覧: 前橋市 |url=https://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/soshiki/kyoiku/bunkazaihogo/gyomu/3/2/5107.html |website=www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp |access-date=2024-06-29 |language=ja}}</ref>
